title: World Bank to Invest in Education for Girls
main_content:
The World Bank Group plans to invest close to $2.5 billion over five years in education projects to help girls between the ages of 12 and 17.

The bank says that about 75 percent of these investments are expected to come from its program for the world’s poorest countries. Most of the countries are in South Asia and in Africa, south of the Sahara. Those areas reportedly have the highest number of out-of-school girls.

The investments were announced by Jim Yong Kim, president of the World Bank Group.

Michelle Obama, the wife of U.S. President Barack Obama, also spoke at the announcement.

She said the investments in education will benefit millions of girls. The First Lady also said it will help build the workforce in each country.

The World Bank says a total of almost 62 million girls around the world are not in school. A World Bank study found that a woman’s lifetime earnings increased by 18 percent for every year she attended school.

questions.question: What will the World Bank Group invest $2.5 billion in?
options: A new healthcare initiative for impoverished countries
Education projects specifically aimed at girls aged 12 to 17
questions.answer: Education projects specifically aimed at girls aged 12 to 17

questions.question: Which countries have the highest number of out-of-school girls?
options: Countries in South America and the Caribbean
South Asian and Sub-Saharan African countries
questions.answer: South Asian and Sub-Saharan African countries

questions.question: What will the investments help to do? What will they help to build?
options: Increase access to higher education and strengthen international relationships
Facilitate vocational training and foster community engagement
Support educational opportunities for girls and build the workforce in each country
Improve literacy rates and develop digital education platforms
questions.answer: Support educational opportunities for girls and build the workforce in each country
